/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Language.RuleEval
  Evaluating a rule over a trace, and checking it before any trace.

  `verdicts` combines the binder classes, the applicability and the obligation per instant
  (Kleene, `verdictAt`). `check` finds from the syntax every defect the evaluator would otherwise
  report as `malformed` or `unboundVariable`; its doc comment lists them. `checkReading`
  names the parameters and aggregates the reading lacks, over the rule and the rules it composes,
  with their concept calls expanded; `Concept.checkReading` the aggregates a concept's body names.

  `Concept.check` holds a concept to the same standard on every admissible instantiation of
  its formals, with its calls expanded. `Concept.callDefects` holds every concept call to the
  callee's signature before expansion loses it.

  Nothing under Rules/ or Concepts/ imports this file; Grounding, Manifest and Monitor do.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Rule
import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Concept
import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Semantics
import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.EvalFast

namespace TrafficSpec
namespace Rule
open Semantics

/-- A rule's formula as evaluated: every comparison over a `cond` decided by cases, through the
    sub-expression cache (`evalFastAll`, whose every stored value is the one `evalAll` gives). -/
def evalRuleFormula (c : SemCtx) (φ : Formula) : Array R := evalFastAll c (Formula.elimCond φ)

/-- Every binder's class holds for its bound track and the applicability holds, per instant. -/
def engagedAll (r : Rule) (c : SemCtx) : Array R :=
  Temporal.allOf c.n (r.binders.map (fun b => evalRuleFormula c b.cls) ++ [evalRuleFormula c r.applicability])

/-- The verdict at every instant. -/
def verdicts (r : Rule) (c : SemCtx) : Array Verdict :=
  Array.zipWith verdictAt (r.engagedAll c) (evalRuleFormula c r.obligation)

/-- The rule as a three-valued statement per instant: complied with (true), violated (false), or
    unknown. Not engaged counts as complied with — a rule that does not apply is not broken. -/
def asRAll (r : Rule) (c : SemCtx) : Array R :=
  (r.verdicts c).map fun v => match v with
    | .compliant | .notApplicable => R.t
    | .violated => R.f
    | .unknown w => ⟨.u, w⟩

/-- Structural well-formedness apart from having a binder: binders named and distinct, the id
    set, every assumption and intention used declared, every intention id well-formed, every
    operationalization bounding its standard by atoms, primitives or concepts. -/
def wellFormedBody (r : Rule) : Bool :=
  r.binderNames.eraseDups.length == r.binders.length &&
  r.binders.all (fun b => !b.name.isEmpty) &&
  !r.id.isEmpty &&
  r.usedAssumptions.all (r.assumptions.contains ·) &&
  r.usedIntentions.all (r.intentions.contains ·) &&
  r.intentions.all IntId.wellFormed &&
  r.operationalizations.all (fun o => !o.concepts.isEmpty && o.concepts.all fun c =>
    c.startsWith "drv." || Primitives.primitiveNames.contains (defName c) || knowsAtom (defName c))

/-- Structural well-formedness: at least one binder, and `wellFormedBody`. -/
def wellFormed (r : Rule) : Bool := !r.binders.isEmpty && r.wellFormedBody

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Static check
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- Variables in scope with their sorts, the innermost first. -/
abbrev Scope := List (String × EntityKind)

/-- Whether `v` is bound and its innermost binding has sort `k`, as evaluation's lookup reads it. -/
def Scope.binds (scope : Scope) (v : String) (k : EntityKind) : Bool :=
  (scope.find? (·.1 == v)).map (·.2) == some k

/-- Resolve arguments against the scope with dummy ids, checking each variable's sort against the
    position's expected sort when the table knows it. An entity position takes a variable only:
    a literal or a number there would name a track, region or device the rule has no right to. -/
private def dummyArgs (scope : Scope) (sorts : Option (List (Option EntityKind))) (args : List Arg)
    : Except String (List Primitives.DArg) :=
  (args.zip (List.range args.length)).mapM fun (a, k) =>
    match a with
    | .var v =>
      match scope.find? (·.1 == v) with

9	  `evalAll` evaluates a formula bottom-up, each subformula once for the whole trace, so a formula
10	  costs O(|φ| · n log n) per binding: atoms map a scene function over the instants, the temporal
11	  operators are the single-pass operators of Temporal.lean, quantifiers evaluate their body once

13

16	  enumeration value or a variable of the wrong sort is `unknown (malformed …)`. The static check
17	  (RuleEval.check) finds every such defect from the syntax before any trace is read, so a checked
18	  rule reports at evaluation time only source absence, truncation, sampling gaps, undefined
19	  concept preconditions, division by zero and unknown compositions.
20	
21	  Finite-trace policy — unobserved is unknown, never compliance:
22	  - `holdsFor` needs its whole window observed at adequate density, else unknown;
23	  - `within`/`untilWithin` are true on a witness, false only when the window is covered;
24	  - `eventually`/`until` carry the unobserved future, `since` the unobserved past, and `always`
25	    the unobserved future as unknown: on a finite trace `always φ` is false or unknown, never true.
26	    A rule's obligation is written for an instant; the sweep over instants (Grounding) is the
27	    "always".
28	
29	  Rule composition is a callback, because the library of rules is defined above this file.

33	import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Intentions

36	namespace Semantics
37

39	open Temporal
40	
41	/-- Everything an evaluation needs: the indexed trace with its reading, the bindings, and how to
42	    evaluate another rule's obligation (`rule id map`) under a variable map, per instant. -/
43	structure SemCtx where
44	  d : Primitives.Ctx
45	  β : Binding := {}
46	  /-- Another rule's verdict per instant under a variable map: complied-with when `engaged` is
47	      false, engaged (classes and applicability) when true. -/
48	  compose : String → List (String × String) → Binding → Bool → Array R :=
49	    fun _ _ _ _ => #[]
50	
51	namespace SemCtx
52	def n (c : SemCtx) : Nat := c.d.n
53	def scenes (c : SemCtx) : Array Scene := c.d.scenes
54	def bindVar (c : SemCtx) (v : String) (x : Val) : SemCtx := { c with β := c.β.bind v x }
55	def mk' (τ : Trace) (ρ : Reading) (β : Binding := {}) : SemCtx := { d := Primitives.Ctx.mk' τ ρ, β := β }
56	end SemCtx
57	
58	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
59	-- Arguments
60	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
61	def resolve (β : Binding) : Arg → Except UnknownReason DArg
62	  | .var v =>
63	    match β.lookup v with

/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Semantics
  The meaning of a formula over a trace: one three-valued result with reasons per instant.

  `evalAll` evaluates a formula bottom-up, each subformula once for the whole trace, so a formula
  costs O(|φ| · n log n) per binding: atoms map a scene function over the instants, the temporal
  operators are the single-pass operators of Temporal.lean, quantifiers evaluate their body once
  per region or device present anywhere in the trace. `eval c i φ` is the value at instant i.

  Atoms and derived concepts are dispatched by name to the definitions of Atoms.lean and
  Primitives.lean; a name the tables do not know, a wrong arity, a literal that spells no
  enumeration value or a variable of the wrong sort is `unknown (malformed …)`. The static check
  (RuleEval.check) finds every such defect from the syntax before any trace is read, so a checked
  rule reports at evaluation time only source absence, truncation, sampling gaps, undefined
  concept preconditions, division by zero and unknown compositions.

  Finite-trace policy — unobserved is unknown, never compliance:
  - `holdsFor` needs its whole window observed at adequate density, else unknown;
  - `within`/`untilWithin` are true on a witness, false only when the window is covered;
  - `eventually`/`until` carry the unobserved future, `since` the unobserved past, and `always`
    the unobserved future as unknown: on a finite trace `always φ` is false or unknown, never true.
    A rule's obligation is written for an instant; the sweep over instants (Grounding) is the
    "always".

  Rule composition is a callback, because the library of rules is defined above this file.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Formula
import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Primitives
import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Intentions

namespace TrafficSpec
namespace Semantics

open Primitives (DArg)
open Temporal

/-- Everything an evaluation needs: the indexed trace with its reading, the bindings, and how to
    evaluate another rule's obligation (`rule id map`) under a variable map, per instant. -/
structure SemCtx where
  d : Primitives.Ctx
  β : Binding := {}
  /-- Another rule's verdict per instant under a variable map: complied-with when `engaged` is
      false, engaged (classes and applicability) when true. -/
  compose : String → List (String × String) → Binding → Bool → Array R :=
    fun _ _ _ _ => #[]

namespace SemCtx
def n (c : SemCtx) : Nat := c.d.n
def scenes (c : SemCtx) : Array Scene := c.d.scenes
def bindVar (c : SemCtx) (v : String) (x : Val) : SemCtx := { c with β := c.β.bind v x }
def mk' (τ : Trace) (ρ : Reading) (β : Binding := {}) : SemCtx := { d := Primitives.Ctx.mk' τ ρ, β := β }
end SemCtx

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Arguments
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def resolve (β : Binding) : Arg → Except UnknownReason DArg
  | .var v =>
    match β.lookup v with
    | some (.track t) => .ok (.v t)
    | some (.region r) => .ok (.v r)
    | some (.device d) => .ok (.v d)
    | none => .error (.unboundVariable v)
  | .lit s => .ok (.s s)
  | .nat k => .ok (.n k)

def resolveAll (β : Binding) (args : List Arg) : Except UnknownReason (List DArg) := args.mapM (resolve β)

private def ent (a : DArg) : Except UnknownReason Nat :=
  match a with | .v t => .ok t | .n k => .ok k | .s _ => .error (.malformed "entity expected")
private def lit (a : DArg) : Except UnknownReason String :=
  match a with | .s s => .ok s | _ => .error (.malformed "literal expected")
private def enumLit {α : Type} (ofString : String → Option α) (a : DArg) : Except UnknownReason α := do
  let s ← lit a
  match ofString s with | some v => .ok v | none => .error (.malformed s)

  b (o.map (· == v)) name
private def q (o : Option Q) (name : String) : QR :=
  match o with | some v => .ok v | none => .error (.absentAtom name)
private def qn (o : Option Nat) (name : String) : QR :=
  match o with | some v => .ok (Q.ofInt (Int.ofNat v)) | none => .error (.absentAtom name)
private def qz (o : Option Int) (name : String) : QR :=
  match o with | some v => .ok (Q.ofInt v) | none => .error (.absentAtom name)

  | "ru_rider_posture_standing_on_deck", [x] => pure (b (ru_rider_posture_standing_on_deck s (← ent x)) name)

  | "st_lane_adjacency", [r, sd, r'] =>
    match sd with
    | .s "left" => pure (b (st_lane_left_of s (← ent r) (← ent r')) name)

  | "st_lane_adjacency_left", [r, r'] => pure (b (st_lane_left_of s (← ent r) (← ent r')) name)
  | "st_lane_adjacency_right", [r, r'] => pure (b (st_lane_right_of s (← ent r) (← ent r')) name)
  | "st_lane_connectivity", [r, r'] => pure (b ((st_lane_connectivity s (← ent r)).map (·.contains (← ent r'))) name)
  | "st_lane_enters", [r, i] => pure (b ((st_lane_enters s (← ent r)).map (· == (← ent i))) name)
  | "st_on_way", [r, w] => pure (b ((st_on_way s (← ent r)).map (·.contains (← ent w))) name)
  | "st_entrance_of", [l, a] => pure (b (st_entrance_of s (← ent l) (← ent a)) name)

    | .s "left" => pure (eqEnum ((st_lane_marking_left s (← ent r)).map (·.1)) (← enumLit MarkingType.ofString t) name)
    | .s "right" => pure (eqEnum ((st_lane_marking_right s (← ent r)).map (·.1)) (← enumLit MarkingType.ofString t) name)
    | _ => .error (.malformed "side")
  | "st_lane_marking", [r, sd, t, col] =>

50	def unit (a : Vec) : Option Vec :=
51	  let m := Q.max (Q.abs a.1) (Q.abs a.2)
52	  if Q.isZero m then none
53	  else
54	    let b := (Q.div a.1 m, Q.div a.2 m)
55	    let n := norm b
56	    some (Q.div b.1 n, Q.div b.2 n)
57	/-- Components of `v` in the frame of heading `h` (longitudinal, lateral); lateral positive = left.
58	    `h` is read as a direction (`unit`), whatever its length; `v` keeps its own. -/
59	def inFrame (h v : Vec) : Option (Q × Q) := do
60	  let u ← unit h
61	  pure (dot u v, cross u v)
62	/-- Distance from a point to a segment. -/
63	def segmentDistance (p a b : Vec) : Q :=
64	  let ab := vsub b a
65	  let ap := vsub p a
66	  let l2 := normSq ab
67	  if Q.isZero l2 then norm ap
68	  else
69	    let t := Q.max Q.zero (Q.min (Q.ofInt 1) (Q.div (dot ap ab) l2))
70	    norm (vsub p (vadd a (Q.mul t ab.1, Q.mul t ab.2)))
71	/-- Whether a point lies inside a polygon (ray casting), for footprint-in-region tests. -/
72	def inPolygon (p : Vec) (poly : List Vec) : Bool :=
73	  let n := poly.length
74	  if n < 3 then false
75	  else
76	    let edges := (List.range n).map fun i => (poly[i]!, poly[(i + 1) % n]!)
77	    let crossings := edges.filter fun (a, b) =>
78	      let (ax, ay) := a; let (bx, by_) := b
79	      ((Q.le ay p.2) != (Q.le by_ p.2)) &&
80	        -- x-intersection of the edge with the horizontal line through p, compared with p.x
81	        (let dy := Q.sub by_ ay
82	         !Q.isZero dy &&
83	         Q.lt p.1 (Q.add ax (Q.div (Q.mul (Q.sub p.2 ay) (Q.sub bx ax)) dy)))
84	    crossings.length % 2 == 1
85	/-- The sign of `(b − a) × (c − a)`: 1 when `c` is to the left of `ab`, −1 to its right, 0 on its line. -/
86	def orient (a b c : Vec) : Int :=
87	  let k := (cross (vsub b a) (vsub c a)).num
88	  if k > 0 then 1 else if k < 0 then -1 else 0
89	/-- Whether `p` lies on the closed segment `ab`, given that it lies on its line. -/
90	def withinBox (p a b : Vec) : Bool :=
91	  Q.le (Q.min a.1 b.1) p.1 && Q.le p.1 (Q.max a.1 b.1) && Q.le (Q.min a.2 b.2) p.2 && Q.le p.2 (Q.max a.2 b.2)
92	/-- Whether the closed segments `ab` and `cd` share a point, touching and collinear overlap included. -/
93	def segmentsIntersect (a b c d : Vec) : Bool :=
94	  let o1 := orient a b c; let o2 := orient a b d; let o3 := orient c d a; let o4 := orient c d b
95	  (o1 * o2 < 0 && o3 * o4 < 0) || (o1 == 0 && withinBox c a b) || (o2 == 0 && withinBox d a b)
96	    || (o3 == 0 && withinBox a c d) || (o4 == 0 && withinBox b c d)
97	/-- The edges of a polygon, the last vertex closing to the first. -/
98	def edges (poly : List Vec) : List (Vec × Vec) :=
99	  let n := poly.length
100	  (List.range n).map fun i => (poly[i]!, poly[(i + 1) % n]!)
101	/-- Whether two polygons share a point as closed sets: an edge of one meets an edge of the other
102	    (touching counts), or one lies inside the other. Exact. -/
103	def polygonsOverlap (p q : List Vec) : Bool :=
104	  (edges p).any (fun (a, b) => (edges q).any fun (c, d) => segmentsIntersect a b c d)
105	    || p.any (inPolygon · q) || q.any (inPolygon · p)
106	/-- Distance from a point to a polygon's boundary: zero inside, the nearest edge outside. -/
107	def polygonDistance (p : Vec) (poly : List Vec) : Option Q :=
108	  match poly with
109	  | [] => none
110	  | [a] => some (norm (vsub p a))
111	  | _ =>
112	    if inPolygon p poly then some Q.zero
113	    else
114	      let n := poly.length
115	      let ds := (List.range n).map fun i => segmentDistance p poly[i]! poly[(i + 1) % n]!
116	      ds.foldl (fun acc d => match acc with | none => some d | some a => some (Q.min a d)) none
117	/-- The point of a segment nearest a point. -/
118	def segmentNearest (p a b : Vec) : Vec :=
119	  let ab := vsub b a
120	  let l2 := normSq ab
121	  if Q.isZero l2 then a
122	  else
123	    let t := Q.max Q.zero (Q.min (Q.ofInt 1) (Q.div (dot (vsub p a) ab) l2))
124	    vadd a (Q.mul t ab.1, Q.mul t ab.2)
125	/-- The point of a polygon's boundary nearest a point. -/
126	def nearestPoint (p : Vec) (poly : List Vec) : Option Vec :=
127	  match poly with
128	  | [] => none
129	  | [a] => some a
130	  | _ =>
131	    let n := poly.length
132	    let cs := (List.range n).map fun i => segmentNearest p poly[i]! poly[(i + 1) % n]!
133	    cs.foldl (fun acc c => match acc with
134	      | none => some c
135	      | some b => if Q.lt (normSq (vsub p c)) (normSq (vsub p b)) then some c else some b) none
136	/-- Every point of a polygon's boundary nearest a point: the nearest point of each edge whose
137	    distance is the least, so a tie keeps every equally near point whatever the vertex order. -/
138	def nearestPoints (p : Vec) (poly : List Vec) : List Vec :=
139	  match poly with
140	  | [] => []
141	  | [a] => [a]
142	  | _ =>
143	    let n := poly.length
144	    let cs := (List.range n).map fun i => segmentNearest p poly[i]! poly[(i + 1) % n]!
145	    match cs.map fun c => normSq (vsub p c) with
146	    | [] => []
147	    | d :: ds =>
148	      let m := ds.foldl Q.min d
149	      cs.filter fun c => Q.eq (normSq (vsub p c)) m
150	/-- The vector from the nearest point of polygon `p` to the nearest point of polygon `q`: zero when
151	    they share a point (`polygonsOverlap`), otherwise the shortest vector joining a vertex of one to
152	    the nearest point of the other's boundary, which for two convex polygons is the same for every
153	    nearest pair. `none` for an empty polygon. -/
154	def nearestOffset (p q : List Vec) : Option Vec :=
155	  if polygonsOverlap p q then some (Q.zero, Q.zero)
156	  else
157	    let fromP := p.filterMap fun c => (nearestPoint c q).map (vsub · c)
158	    let fromQ := q.filterMap fun c => (nearestPoint c p).map (vsub c ·)
159	    (fromP ++ fromQ).foldl (fun acc d => match acc with
160	      | none => some d
161	      | some e => if Q.lt (normSq d) (normSq e) then some d else some e) none
162	/-- The interval a polygon covers along the direction `u`, measured from `o`: (lowest, highest). -/
163	def span (u o : Vec) (poly : List Vec) : Option (Q × Q) :=
164	  match poly.map fun c => dot u (vsub c o) with
165	  | [] => none
166	  | x :: xs => some (xs.foldl Q.min x, xs.foldl Q.max x)
167	/-- Twice the signed area of a polygon (the shoelace sum). -/
168	def area2 (poly : List Vec) : Q :=
169	  (edges poly).foldl (fun acc (a, b) => Q.add acc (cross a b)) Q.zero
170	/-- Whether a polygon's boundary crosses or touches itself: two edges that are not neighbours
171	    meet, or two neighbouring edges fold back along one line. -/
172	def selfIntersects (poly : List Vec) : Bool :=
173	  let es := (edges poly).toArray
174	  let n := es.size
175	  (List.range n).any fun i => (List.range n).any fun j =>
176	    if j ≤ i then false
177	    else
178	      let (a, b) := es[i]!
179	      let (c, d) := es[j]!
180	      if j == i + 1 then orient a b d == 0 && Q.lt (dot (vsub b a) (vsub d c)) Q.zero
181	      else if i == 0 && j + 1 == n then orient c d b == 0 && Q.lt (dot (vsub d c) (vsub b a)) Q.zero
182	      else segmentsIntersect a b c d
183	/-- A simple polygon: at least three vertices, a non-zero area, and a boundary that neither crosses
184	    nor touches itself (a repeated vertex makes two edges that are not neighbours meet). -/
185	def simplePolygon (poly : List Vec) : Bool :=
186	  poly.length ≥ 3 && !Q.isZero (area2 poly) && !selfIntersects poly
187	/-- Whether a point lies on a polygon's boundary. Exact. -/
188	def onBoundary (p : Vec) (poly : List Vec) : Bool :=
189	  (edges poly).any fun (a, b) => orient a b p == 0 && withinBox p a b
190	/-- The parameters `t` at which the line `p + t·u` meets the polygon's boundary: one per edge it
191	    crosses or touches, and both ends of an edge it runs along. `u` is not the zero vector. -/
192	def lineCrossings (p u : Vec) (poly : List Vec) : List Q :=
193	  (edges poly).flatMap fun (a, b) =>
194	    let d := vsub b a
195	    let w := vsub a p
196	    let den := cross u d
197	    if Q.isZero den then
198	      if Q.isZero (cross u w) then [Q.div (dot w u) (dot u u), Q.div (dot (vsub b p) u) (dot u u)] else []
199	    else
200	      let s := Q.div (cross w u) den
201	      if Q.le Q.zero s && Q.le s (Q.ofInt 1) then [Q.div (cross w d) den] else []
202	end Geom

277	/-- Whether kind `a` refines kind `b`, reflexively and transitively. -/
278	def StructureKind.refines (a b : StructureKind) : Bool := a == b || a.ancestors.contains b
279	
280	/-- Whether a source that cannot tell kind `m` (it is among `unobservedKinds`) leaves this structure's
281	    membership of `m`'s kinds open: always where `m` refines no kind other than an abstract one;
282	    otherwise only where the structure is labelled `m` or a kind `m` refines, since a structure of any
283	    other kind is known not to be one. -/
284	def Structure.maskApplies (st : Structure) (m : StructureKind) : Bool :=
285	  (m.parent?.filter (!·.isAbstract)).isNone || m.refines st.kind
286	
287	/-- Whether a structure is of kind `k`: unknown where a kind the source cannot tell, applying to this
288	    structure, is `k` or a kind `k` refines (the label cannot be trusted for `k`); true where the
289	    structure's kind refines `k`; unknown where a kind the source cannot tell, applying to this
290	    structure, refines `k`; false otherwise. A parent never implies a kind refining it, two kinds
291	    refining one parent never imply each other, and a kind the source cannot tell never makes a known
292	    parent unknown. An abstract kind is the union of the kinds refining it: true where the structure
293	    is of one of them, unknown where it is of none and unknown for one, false otherwise. -/
294	def Structure.isOfKind (st : Structure) (k : StructureKind) : Option Bool :=
295	  let masked := st.unobservedKinds.filter st.maskApplies
296	  let concrete (k : StructureKind) : Option Bool :=
297	    if masked.any (k.refines ·) then none
298	    else if st.kind.refines k then some true
299	    else if masked.any (·.refines k) then none
300	    else some false
301	  if k.isAbstract then
302	    let vs := (StructureKind.all.filter (·.parent? == some k)).map concrete
303	    if vs.contains (some true) then some true else if vs.contains none then none else some false
304	  else concrete k

def norm (a : Vec) : Q := sqrtMicro (normSq a)
/-- The unit vector along `a`; `none` for the zero vector only. `a` is first divided by its larger
    absolute component, so the vector normalised has length between 1 and √2 whatever `a`'s scale,
    and then by that length taken to micrometres (`norm`). The result is the exact unit vector times
    a factor of at least 1 and below 1 + 2·10⁻⁶, and is exact where the scaled length is a whole
    number of micrometres (every axis-aligned direction). -/
def unit (a : Vec) : Option Vec :=
  let m := Q.max (Q.abs a.1) (Q.abs a.2)
  if Q.isZero m then none
  else
    let b := (Q.div a.1 m, Q.div a.2 m)
    let n := norm b
    some (Q.div b.1 n, Q.div b.2 n)
/-- Components of `v` in the frame of heading `h` (longitudinal, lateral); lateral positive = left.
    `h` is read as a direction (`unit`), whatever its length; `v` keeps its own. -/
def inFrame (h v : Vec) : Option (Q × Q) := do
  let u ← unit h
  pure (dot u v, cross u v)
/-- Distance from a point to a segment. -/
def segmentDistance (p a b : Vec) : Q :=
  let ab := vsub b a
  let ap := vsub p a
  let l2 := normSq ab
  if Q.isZero l2 then norm ap
  else
    let t := Q.max Q.zero (Q.min (Q.ofInt 1) (Q.div (dot ap ab) l2))
    norm (vsub p (vadd a (Q.mul t ab.1, Q.mul t ab.2)))
/-- Whether a point lies inside a polygon (ray casting), for footprint-in-region tests. -/
def inPolygon (p : Vec) (poly : List Vec) : Bool :=
  let n := poly.length
  if n < 3 then false
  else
    let edges := (List.range n).map fun i => (poly[i]!, poly[(i + 1) % n]!)
    let crossings := edges.filter fun (a, b) =>
      let (ax, ay) := a; let (bx, by_) := b
      ((Q.le ay p.2) != (Q.le by_ p.2)) &&
        -- x-intersection of the edge with the horizontal line through p, compared with p.x
        (let dy := Q.sub by_ ay
         !Q.isZero dy &&
         Q.lt p.1 (Q.add ax (Q.div (Q.mul (Q.sub p.2 ay) (Q.sub bx ax)) dy)))
    crossings.length % 2 == 1
/-- The sign of `(b − a) × (c − a)`: 1 when `c` is to the left of `ab`, −1 to its right, 0 on its line. -/
def orient (a b c : Vec) : Int :=
  let k := (cross (vsub b a) (vsub c a)).num
  if k > 0 then 1 else if k < 0 then -1 else 0
/-- Whether `p` lies on the closed segment `ab`, given that it lies on its line. -/
def withinBox (p a b : Vec) : Bool :=
  Q.le (Q.min a.1 b.1) p.1 && Q.le p.1 (Q.max a.1 b.1) && Q.le (Q.min a.2 b.2) p.2 && Q.le p.2 (Q.max a.2 b.2)
/-- Whether the closed segments `ab` and `cd` share a point, touching and collinear overlap included. -/
def segmentsIntersect (a b c d : Vec) : Bool :=
  let o1 := orient a b c; let o2 := orient a b d; let o3 := orient c d a; let o4 := orient c d b
  (o1 * o2 < 0 && o3 * o4 < 0) || (o1 == 0 && withinBox c a b) || (o2 == 0 && withinBox d a b)
    || (o3 == 0 && withinBox a c d) || (o4 == 0 && withinBox b c d)
/-- The edges of a polygon, the last vertex closing to the first. -/
def edges (poly : List Vec) : List (Vec × Vec) :=
  let n := poly.length
  (List.range n).map fun i => (poly[i]!, poly[(i + 1) % n]!)
/-- Whether two polygons share a point as closed sets: an edge of one meets an edge of the other
    (touching counts), or one lies inside the other. Exact. -/
def polygonsOverlap (p q : List Vec) : Bool :=
  (edges p).any (fun (a, b) => (edges q).any fun (c, d) => segmentsIntersect a b c d)
    || p.any (inPolygon · q) || q.any (inPolygon · p)
/-- Distance from a point to a polygon's boundary: zero inside, the nearest edge outside. -/
def polygonDistance (p : Vec) (poly : List Vec) : Option Q :=
  match poly with
  | [] => none
  | [a] => some (norm (vsub p a))
  | _ =>
    if inPolygon p poly then some Q.zero
    else
      let n := poly.length
      let ds := (List.range n).map fun i => segmentDistance p poly[i]! poly[(i + 1) % n]!
      ds.foldl (fun acc d => match acc with | none => some d | some a => some (Q.min a d)) none
/-- The point of a segment nearest a point. -/
def segmentNearest (p a b : Vec) : Vec :=
  let ab := vsub b a
  let l2 := normSq ab
  if Q.isZero l2 then a
  else
    let t := Q.max Q.zero (Q.min (Q.ofInt 1) (Q.div (dot (vsub p a) ab) l2))
    vadd a (Q.mul t ab.1, Q.mul t ab.2)
/-- The point of a polygon's boundary nearest a point. -/
def nearestPoint (p : Vec) (poly : List Vec) : Option Vec :=
  match poly with
  | [] => none
  | [a] => some a
  | _ =>
    let n := poly.length
    let cs := (List.range n).map fun i => segmentNearest p poly[i]! poly[(i + 1) % n]!
    cs.foldl (fun acc c => match acc with
      | none => some c
      | some b => if Q.lt (normSq (vsub p c)) (normSq (vsub p b)) then some c else some b) none
/-- Every point of a polygon's boundary nearest a point: the nearest point of each edge whose
    distance is the least, so a tie keeps every equally near point whatever the vertex order. -/
def nearestPoints (p : Vec) (poly : List Vec) : List Vec :=
  match poly with
  | [] => []
  | [a] => [a]
  | _ =>
    let n := poly.length
    let cs := (List.range n).map fun i => segmentNearest p poly[i]! poly[(i + 1) % n]!
    match cs.map fun c => normSq (vsub p c) with
    | [] => []
    | d :: ds =>
      let m := ds.foldl Q.min d
      cs.filter fun c => Q.eq (normSq (vsub p c)) m
/-- The vector from the nearest point of polygon `p` to the nearest point of polygon `q`: zero when
    they share a point (`polygonsOverlap`), otherwise the shortest vector joining a vertex of one to
    the nearest point of the other's boundary, which for two convex polygons is the same for every
    nearest pair. `none` for an empty polygon. -/
def nearestOffset (p q : List Vec) : Option Vec :=
  if polygonsOverlap p q then some (Q.zero, Q.zero)
  else
    let fromP := p.filterMap fun c => (nearestPoint c q).map (vsub · c)
    let fromQ := q.filterMap fun c => (nearestPoint c p).map (vsub c ·)
    (fromP ++ fromQ).foldl (fun acc d => match acc with
      | none => some d
      | some e => if Q.lt (normSq d) (normSq e) then some d else some e) none
/-- The interval a polygon covers along the direction `u`, measured from `o`: (lowest, highest). -/
def span (u o : Vec) (poly : List Vec) : Option (Q × Q) :=
  match poly.map fun c => dot u (vsub c o) with
  | [] => none
  | x :: xs => some (xs.foldl Q.min x, xs.foldl Q.max x)
/-- Twice the signed area of a polygon (the shoelace sum). -/
def area2 (poly : List Vec) : Q :=
  (edges poly).foldl (fun acc (a, b) => Q.add acc (cross a b)) Q.zero
/-- Whether a polygon's boundary crosses or touches itself: two edges that are not neighbours
    meet, or two neighbouring edges fold back along one line. -/
def selfIntersects (poly : List Vec) : Bool :=
  let es := (edges poly).toArray
  let n := es.size
  (List.range n).any fun i => (List.range n).any fun j =>
    if j ≤ i then false
    else
      let (a, b) := es[i]!
      let (c, d) := es[j]!
      if j == i + 1 then orient a b d == 0 && Q.lt (dot (vsub b a) (vsub d c)) Q.zero
      else if i == 0 && j + 1 == n then orient c d b == 0 && Q.lt (dot (vsub d c) (vsub b a)) Q.zero
      else segmentsIntersect a b c d
/-- A simple polygon: at least three vertices, a non-zero area, and a boundary that neither crosses
    nor touches itself (a repeated vertex makes two edges that are not neighbours meet). -/
def simplePolygon (poly : List Vec) : Bool :=
  poly.length ≥ 3 && !Q.isZero (area2 poly) && !selfIntersects poly
/-- Whether a point lies on a polygon's boundary. Exact. -/
def onBoundary (p : Vec) (poly : List Vec) : Bool :=
  (edges poly).any fun (a, b) => orient a b p == 0 && withinBox p a b
/-- The parameters `t` at which the line `p + t·u` meets the polygon's boundary: one per edge it
    crosses or touches, and both ends of an edge it runs along. `u` is not the zero vector. -/
def lineCrossings (p u : Vec) (poly : List Vec) : List Q :=
  (edges poly).flatMap fun (a, b) =>
    let d := vsub b a
    let w := vsub a p
    let den := cross u d
    if Q.isZero den then
      if Q.isZero (cross u w) then [Q.div (dot w u) (dot u u), Q.div (dot (vsub b p) u) (dot u u)] else []
    else
      let s := Q.div (cross w u) den
      if Q.le Q.zero s && Q.le s (Q.ofInt 1) then [Q.div (cross w d) den] else []
end Geom

/-- Whether kind `a` refines kind `b`, reflexively and transitively. -/
def StructureKind.refines (a b : StructureKind) : Bool := a == b || a.ancestors.contains b

/-- Whether a source that cannot tell kind `m` (it is among `unobservedKinds`) leaves this structure's
    membership of `m`'s kinds open: always where `m` refines no kind other than an abstract one;
    otherwise only where the structure is labelled `m` or a kind `m` refines, since a structure of any
    other kind is known not to be one. -/
def Structure.maskApplies (st : Structure) (m : StructureKind) : Bool :=
  (m.parent?.filter (!·.isAbstract)).isNone || m.refines st.kind

/-- Whether a structure is of kind `k`: unknown where a kind the source cannot tell, applying to this
    structure, is `k` or a kind `k` refines (the label cannot be trusted for `k`); true where the
    structure's kind refines `k`; unknown where a kind the source cannot tell, applying to this
    structure, refines `k`; false otherwise. A parent never implies a kind refining it, two kinds
    refining one parent never imply each other, and a kind the source cannot tell never makes a known
    parent unknown. An abstract kind is the union of the kinds refining it: true where the structure
    is of one of them, unknown where it is of none and unknown for one, false otherwise. -/
def Structure.isOfKind (st : Structure) (k : StructureKind) : Option Bool :=
  let masked := st.unobservedKinds.filter st.maskApplies
  let concrete (k : StructureKind) : Option Bool :=
    if masked.any (k.refines ·) then none
    else if st.kind.refines k then some true
    else if masked.any (·.refines k) then none
    else some false
  if k.isAbstract then
    let vs := (StructureKind.all.filter (·.parent? == some k)).map concrete
    if vs.contains (some true) then some true else if vs.contains none then none else some false
  else concrete k

/-- Whether a region is of a kind (`Structure.isOfKind`); unknown for a region not in the scene. -/
def isKind (s : Scene) (r : RegionId) (k : StructureKind) : Option Bool :=
  (s.structure? r).bind (·.isOfKind k)

    | some o, some n => if o == n then some false else none

/-- The rectangle a road user's body covers on the ground, from its position, heading and
    half-extents; `none` when one of them is not observed. -/
def footprint (s : Scene) (x : TrackId) : Option (List Vec) := do
  let p ← kin_position s x
  let h ← kin_heading s x
  let (hl, hw, _) ← kin_extent s x
  let u ← Geom.unit h
  let v := (Q.neg u.2, u.1)
  let corner (a b : Q) : Vec := Geom.vadd p (Q.add (Q.mul a u.1) (Q.mul b v.1), Q.add (Q.mul a u.2) (Q.mul b v.2))
  pure [corner hl hw, corner hl (Q.neg hw), corner (Q.neg hl) (Q.neg hw), corner (Q.neg hl) hw]

/-- Ground distance from a road user's body to a region: zero when the footprint overlaps the
    boundary, otherwise the nearest approach between the two outlines. Without a footprint (no
    extent or heading observed) the reference point is used; a point-like structure is measured
    to its reference point. -/
def st_region_geometry_distance (s : Scene) (x : TrackId) (r : RegionId) : Option Q := do
  let p ← kin_position s x
  match st_region_geometry_boundary s r, footprint s x with
  | some poly, some fp =>
    if Geom.polygonsOverlap fp poly then some Q.zero
    else
      let ds := fp.filterMap (Geom.polygonDistance · poly) ++ poly.filterMap (Geom.polygonDistance · fp)
      ds.foldl (fun acc d => match acc with | none => some d | some a => some (Q.min a d)) none
  | some poly, none => Geom.polygonDistance p poly
  | none, fp =>
    let c ← st_region_geometry_position s r
    match fp with
    | some poly => Geom.polygonDistance c poly
    | none => some (Geom.norm (Geom.vsub c p))

  (s.structures.filter (·.isOfKind k == some true)).map (·.id)
/-- The regions a quantifier over a kind ranges over: those whose membership of the kind is not
    false (`Structure.isOfKind`), the known members and those that may be members. -/
def regionCandidates (s : Scene) (k : StructureKind) : List RegionId :=
  (s.structures.filter (·.isOfKind k != some false)).map (·.id)

import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.World

namespace TrafficSpec

/-- Well-formed intention id: `int.` followed by a snake-case name. -/

    pair or the id is not declared. -/

/-- s8: some travel region that is i or enters i is governed by a traffic signal, stop sign or yield sign. -/
def governedBy (kind : String) : Formula :=
  .existsDevice (.lit kind) "d" (.atom "dev_governs" [.var "d", .var "r"] [])

def controlled : Formula :=
  .existsRegion (.lit "travel_region") "r"
    (.and (.or (.same (.var "r") vI) (enters (.var "r") vI))
      (orAll [governedBy "traffic_signal", governedBy "stop_sign", governedBy "yield_sign"]))

/-- s8 with s7's `unless` compositions conjoined. -/
def s8 : Formula :=
  andAll [ controlled
         , .not (.ruleApplies "NRS_484B_250_4_o1" [("x", "x")])
         , .not (.ruleApplies "NRS_484B_250_4_o2" [("x", "x")]) ]

def dir (r : Arg) (k : String) : Term := .measure "st_lane_direction" [r, .lit k]

/-- s9: the designated directions of c and cy are opposite. -/
def opposed : Formula :=
  .cmp (.add (.mul (dir vC "x") (dir vCy "x")) (.mul (dir vC "y") (dir vCy "y")))
    .lt (.neg pOpposedApproachCosTolerance)

def turningLeftIn (u : Arg) : Formula :=
  .and (.derived "drv_motion_turning_left" [u] [pYawRateTolerance]) (occupies u vI)

/-- s9–s11: opposite approaches with x or y intending or making a left turn at i. -/
def leftTurnException : Formula :=
  .and opposed
    (orAll [ .intent "int.turn_left" vX vI
           , .intent "int.turn_left" vY vI
           , turningLeftIn vX
           , turningLeftIn vY ])

/-- s6: cy lies on a highway c does not lie on. -/
def differentHighway : Formula :=
  .existsRegion (.lit "highway") "h"
    (.and (.atom "st_on_way" [vCy, .var "h"] []) (.not (.atom "st_on_way" [vC, .var "h"] [])))

/-- s5, s6, s9–s11: y, not x, a vehicle that has entered i from a carrier on a different highway,
    not excepted. -/
def enteredVehicle : Formula :=
  andAll [ .not (.same vX vY)
         , vehicle vY
         , occupies vY vI
         , .existsRegion (.lit "travel_region") "cy"
             (andAll [ notIntersection vCy
                     , .since (occupies vY vI) (.and (occupies vY vCy) (enters vCy vI))
                     , differentHighway
                     , .not leftTurnException ]) ]

/-- s4: the danger of a crash between x and y. -/
def conflict : Formula :=
  .and (.derived "prim_closest_approach_within" [vX, vY] [pConflictTimeHorizon])
    (.cmp (.quantity "prim_closest_approach_distance" [vX, vY] [pConflictTimeHorizon]) .lt
      pConflictCentreClearance)

def clsX : Formula := vehicle vX

/-- Applicability: s2 (trigger): approaching an intersection; s5 (condition): to a vehicle which has entered the intersection; s6 (condition): from a different highway.; s8 (exception): this section does not apply at intersections controlled by official traffic-control devices; s9 (exception): or to vehicles approaching each other from opposite directions,; s10 (exception): when the driver of one of the vehicles is intending to; s11 (exception): or is making a left turn. -/
def applicability : Formula :=
  .existsRegion (.lit "travel_region") "c"
    (.existsRegion (.lit "intersection") "i"
      (andAll [approaches, .not s8, .existsUser "y" enteredVehicle]))

/-- Obligation: s3 (obligation): shall yield; s4 (standard): the right-of-way -/
def obligation : Formula :=
  .forallRegion (.lit "travel_region") "c"
    (.forallRegion (.lit "intersection") "i"
      (.implies
        (andAll [ approaches, .not s8, occupies vX vI
                , .derived "drv_motion_moving" [vX] [pMotionSpeedTolerance] ])
        (.forallUser "y" (.implies enteredVehicle (.not conflict)))))

/-
  Witnesses for NRS_484B_250_1.

  Geometry (metres, +x east, +y north): intersection i (10) is the square [-5, 5] × [-5, 5], lying on
  highways A (20, west of it), B (21, north–south) and C (22, east of it). Approach carriers, each
  entering i: cA (11) eastbound, x ∈ [-60, -5], y ∈ [-5, 0], on A; cB (12) northbound, x ∈ [0, 5],
  y ∈ [-60, -5], on B; cW (13) westbound, x ∈ [5, 60], y ∈ [0, 5], on C (A changes name to C across
  the junction, so cW is opposed to cA yet on a different highway).
  x (track 1) is a 4 m × 2 m car eastbound on cA at y = -2.5; y (track 2) is a car of the same size.
  Instants 1 s apart. A body across two regions has the second one stated in `occupies`.
  At x's entry (x at -4.5, 5 m/s) with y at (2.5, -4.5) northbound at 2 m/s, the predicted closest
  approach is about 0.74 m after about 1.34 s: well inside 4 m and 3 s. In the opposed scenes y
  runs westbound at y = 2.5, 5 m laterally from x: no conflict there, the exception decides.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Rules.NRS_484B.NRS_484B_250_1
import TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Builders

namespace TrafficSpecWitness.NRS_484B_250_1

open TrafficSpec

def m (n : Int) : Q := Units.metres n
def cm (n : Int) : Q := Units.centimetres n

-- Binders ↦ tracks: x ↦ 1

def iR : Structure :=
  { Build.rect 10 .intersection (m (-5)) (m (-5)) (m 5) (m 5) with ways := some [20, 21, 22] }
def cA : Structure :=
  { Build.lane 11 [(m (-60), m (-5)), (m (-5), m (-5)), (m (-5), m 0), (m (-60), m 0)] Build.east
      (enters := some 10) with ways := some [20] }
def cB : Structure :=
  { Build.lane 12 [(m 0, m (-60)), (m 5, m (-60)), (m 5, m (-5)), (m 0, m (-5))] Build.north
      (enters := some 10) with ways := some [21] }
def cW : Structure :=
  { Build.lane 13 [(m 5, m 0), (m 60, m 0), (m 60, m 5), (m 5, m 5)] Build.west
      (enters := some 10) with ways := some [22] }
def hA : Structure := Build.rect 20 .highway (m (-100)) (m (-5)) (m 5) (m 5)
def hB : Structure := Build.rect 21 .highway (m (-5)) (m (-100)) (m 5) (m 100)
def hC : Structure := Build.rect 22 .highway (m 5) (m (-5)) (m 100) (m 5)

def structs : List Structure := [iR, cA, cB, cW, hA, hB, hC]

def withYaw (u : RoadUser) (yaw : Q) : RoadUser :=
  Build.withKin u (fun k => { k with yawRate := some yaw })

/-- x eastbound on cA at y = -2.5. -/
def xAt (px : Q) (speed : Int) (yaw : Int := 0) : RoadUser :=
  withYaw (Build.user 1 [.motorVehicle] (px, cm (-250)) Build.east (Units.metresPerSecond speed) (m 2, m 1, m 1))
    (Units.degrees yaw)
/-- y northbound on cB at x = 2.5. -/
def yNorth (py : Q) (speed : Int) : RoadUser :=
  withYaw (Build.user 2 [.motorVehicle] (cm 250, py) Build.north (Units.metresPerSecond speed) (m 2, m 1, m 1))
    (Units.degrees 0)
/-- y westbound on cW at y = 2.5. -/
def yWest (px : Q) (speed : Int) (yaw : Int := 0) : RoadUser :=
  withYaw (Build.user 2 [.motorVehicle] (px, cm 250) Build.west (Units.metresPerSecond speed) (m 2, m 1, m 1))
    (Units.degrees yaw)

def mkScene (t : Timestamp) (users : List RoadUser) (devices : List Device)
    (extra : List (TrackId × RegionId)) (intents : List DeclaredIntent := []) : Scene :=
  Build.scene t (some 1) users structs devices
    (occupies := some (Build.occupancyFromGeometry users structs ++ extra)) (intents := intents)

def turnLeft (who : TrackId) (v : Bool) : DeclaredIntent :=
  { vehicle := who, target := 10, values := [("int.turn_left", v)] }

/-- x on cA moving into i (entry at instant 2); y entered i from cB at instant 1 and crosses. -/
def crossingTrace (devices : List Device) : Trace :=
  Build.trace 3 0 (Units.seconds 1) fun k t =>
    match k with
    | 0 => mkScene t [xAt (cm (-1450)) 5, yNorth (cm (-850)) 2] devices []
    | 1 => mkScene t [xAt (cm (-950)) 5, yNorth (cm (-650)) 2] devices [(2, 10)]
    | _ => mkScene t [xAt (cm (-450)) 5, yNorth (cm (-450)) 2] devices [(1, 11), (2, 12)]

/-- `forbid` (violated): No device governs i or its approaches. x approaches on lane c (st.lane_enters c i, on highway A); y entered i from lane cy on highway B and is crossing. x moves into i; predicted closest approach 1 m in 1.5 s. -/
def forbidTrace : Trace := crossingTrace []

/-- `permit` (compliant): Same, but x halts on c while y crosses i and enters only after y has left. -/
def permitTrace : Trace :=
  Build.trace 5 0 (Units.seconds 1) fun k t =>
    match k with
    | 0 => mkScene t [xAt (cm (-1450)) 5, yNorth (cm (-850)) 4] [] []
    | 1 => mkScene t [xAt (cm (-950)) 0, yNorth (cm (-450)) 4] [] [(2, 12)]
    | 2 => mkScene t [xAt (cm (-950)) 0, yNorth (cm (-50)) 4] [] []
    | 3 => mkScene t [xAt (cm (-950)) 0, yNorth (cm 350) 4] [] []
    | _ => mkScene t [xAt (cm (-450)) 5, yNorth (cm 750) 4] [] [(1, 11)]

/-- `idle` (not_applicable): A dev.stop_sign governs c; the intersection is controlled by an official device and no signal is inoperative. -/
def idleTrace : Trace := crossingTrace [Build.sign 30 .stopSign [11]]

/-- `blind` (unknown): As forbid, but st.lane_enters is not observed, so whether x approaches i and from which carrier y entered is unknown. -/
def blindTrace : Trace := crossingTrace []

/-- y westbound on cW (opposed to cA): `yPos`, `yYaw` and the declarations per instant. -/
def opposedTrace (yPos : Nat → Q) (ySpeed : Int) (yYaw xYaw : Nat → Int)
    (yExtra : Nat → List (TrackId × RegionId)) (intents : List DeclaredIntent) : Trace :=
  Build.trace 3 0 (Units.seconds 1) fun k t =>
    let xPos := match k with | 0 => cm (-1450) | 1 => cm (-950) | _ => cm (-450)
    let xExtra : List (TrackId × RegionId) := if k ≥ 2 then [(1, 11)] else []
    mkScene t [xAt xPos 5 (xYaw k), yWest (yPos k) ySpeed (yYaw k)] [] (xExtra ++ yExtra k) intents

/-- `branch_1` (not_applicable): x and y approach on opposed carriers (dot product of directions -1); y has int.turn_left at i and is turning left within i when x moves in: y is excepted and no other vehicle has entered i. At instant 1 y is in i declaring the turn but not yet turning. -/
def branch_1Trace : Trace :=
  opposedTrace (fun k => match k with | 0 => cm 850 | 1 => cm 650 | _ => cm 450) 2
    (fun k => if k ≥ 2 then 10 else 0) (fun _ => 0)
    (fun k => match k with | 0 => [] | 1 => [(2, 10)] | _ => [(2, 13)])
    [turnLeft 2 true]

/-- `branch_2` (violated): i is governed by a dev.traffic_signal that is dev.inoperative at x's entry; the device exception is suspended; y crossing from highway B, conflict predicted when x moves in. -/
def branch_2Trace : Trace :=
  crossingTrace [{ Build.signal 30 [10, 11, 12] [.dark] with inoperative := some true, uncovered := some true }]

/-- `branch_3` (not_applicable): x approaches and enters an uncontrolled intersection with no other road user in the scene. -/
def branch_3Trace : Trace :=
  Build.trace 3 0 (Units.seconds 1) fun k t =>
    match k with
    | 0 => mkScene t [xAt (cm (-1450)) 5] [] []
    | 1 => mkScene t [xAt (cm (-950)) 5] [] []
    | _ => mkScene t [xAt (cm (-450)) 5] [] [(1, 11)]

/-- `branch_4` (not_applicable): opposed approaches; y, declaring nothing, is turning left within i
    from its entry: the turn alone excepts it. -/
def branch_4Trace : Trace :=
  opposedTrace (fun k => match k with | 0 => cm 850 | 1 => cm 650 | _ => cm 450) 2
    (fun k => if k ≥ 1 then 10 else 0) (fun _ => 0)
    (fun k => match k with | 0 => [] | 1 => [(2, 10)] | _ => [(2, 13)])
    []

/-- `branch_5` (not_applicable): opposed approaches; x declares int.turn_left at i, y declares no
    left turn and goes straight: x's intention excepts y. -/
def branch_5Trace : Trace :=
  opposedTrace (fun k => match k with | 0 => cm 850 | 1 => cm 650 | _ => cm 450) 2
    (fun _ => 0) (fun _ => 0)
    (fun k => match k with | 0 => [] | 1 => [(2, 10)] | _ => [(2, 13)])
    [turnLeft 1 true, turnLeft 2 false]

/-- `branch_6` (not_applicable): opposed approaches, neither declaring a left turn; y reaches i at
    the instant x enters it turning left: x's turn within i excepts y. -/
def branch_6Trace : Trace :=
  opposedTrace (fun k => match k with | 0 => cm 1450 | 1 => cm 1050 | _ => cm 650) 4
    (fun _ => 0) (fun k => if k ≥ 2 then 10 else 0)
    (fun k => match k with | 0 => [] | 1 => [] | _ => [(2, 10)])
    [turnLeft 1 false, turnLeft 2 false]

/-- `branch_7` (not_applicable): as forbid, but a yield sign governs i itself. -/
def branch_7Trace : Trace := crossingTrace [Build.sign 30 .yieldSign [10]]

/-- `branch_8` (not_applicable): as forbid, but an operating traffic signal governs i and its approaches. -/
def branch_8Trace : Trace :=
  crossingTrace [{ Build.signal 30 [10, 11, 12] [.circularGreen] with inoperative := some false, uncovered := some true }]

def witness (name : String) (τ : Trace) (expected : Verdict)
    (absent : List String := []) (boundary : String := "") : Scenario :=
  { name := name
    rule := "NRS_484B_250_1"
    trace := τ
    reading := {}          -- ignored by the gate: the run's reading is substituted
    manifest := Build.manifest absent
    grounding := [("x", 1)]
    expected := expected
    boundary := boundary }

def scenarios : List Scenario :=
  [ witness "forbid" forbidTrace .violated
  , witness "permit" permitTrace .compliant
  , witness "idle" idleTrace .notApplicable
  , witness "blind" blindTrace (.unknown []) ["st.lane_enters"]
  , witness "branch_1" branch_1Trace .notApplicable
  , witness "branch_2" branch_2Trace .violated
  , witness "branch_3" branch_3Trace .notApplicable
  , witness "branch_4" branch_4Trace .notApplicable
  , witness "branch_5" branch_5Trace .notApplicable
  , witness "branch_6" branch_6Trace .notApplicable
  , witness "branch_7" branch_7Trace .notApplicable
  , witness "branch_8" branch_8Trace .notApplicable ]

end TrafficSpecWitness.NRS_484B_250_1

  y ∈ [-60, -5], on B; cW (13) westbound, x ∈ [5, 60], y ∈ [0, 5], on C (A changes name to C across
  the junction, so cW is opposed to cA yet on a different highway).
  x (track 1) is a 4 m × 2 m car eastbound on cA at y = -2.5; y (track 2) is a car of the same size.

  approach is about 0.74 m after about 1.34 s: well inside 4 m and 3 s. In the opposed scenes y
  runs westbound at y = 2.5, 5 m laterally from x: no conflict there, the exception decides.
-/

import TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Builders

open TrafficSpec

def m (n : Int) : Q := Units.metres n
def cm (n : Int) : Q := Units.centimetres n

def iR : Structure :=
  { Build.rect 10 .intersection (m (-5)) (m (-5)) (m 5) (m 5) with ways := some [20, 21, 22] }
def cA : Structure :=
  { Build.lane 11 [(m (-60), m (-5)), (m (-5), m (-5)), (m (-5), m 0), (m (-60), m 0)] Build.east
      (enters := some 10) with ways := some [20] }
def cB : Structure :=
  { Build.lane 12 [(m 0, m (-60)), (m 5, m (-60)), (m 5, m (-5)), (m 0, m (-5))] Build.north
      (enters := some 10) with ways := some [21] }
def cW : Structure :=
  { Build.lane 13 [(m 5, m 0), (m 60, m 0), (m 60, m 5), (m 5, m 5)] Build.west
      (enters := some 10) with ways := some [22] }
def hA : Structure := Build.rect 20 .highway (m (-100)) (m (-5)) (m 5) (m 5)
def hB : Structure := Build.rect 21 .highway (m (-5)) (m (-100)) (m 5) (m 100)
def hC : Structure := Build.rect 22 .highway (m 5) (m (-5)) (m 100) (m 5)

def structs : List Structure := [iR, cA, cB, cW, hA, hB, hC]

def withYaw (u : RoadUser) (yaw : Q) : RoadUser :=
  Build.withKin u (fun k => { k with yawRate := some yaw })

/-- A unit heading given to 10⁻⁸ (cosine, sine of its angle). -/
def hdg (c s : Int) : Vec := (Units.ratio c 100000000, Units.ratio s 100000000)
/-- East turned 10° to the left; west turned 10° and 20° to the left. -/
def east10 : Vec := hdg 98480775 17364818
def west10 : Vec := hdg (-98480775) (-17364818)
def west20 : Vec := hdg (-93969262) (-34202014)

    | 1 => mkScene t [xAt (cm (-950)) 0, yNorth (cm (-450)) 4] [] [(2, 12)]
    | 2 => mkScene t [xAt (cm (-950)) 0, yNorth (cm (-50)) 4] [] []
    | 3 => mkScene t [xAt (cm (-950)) 0, yNorth (cm 350) 4] [] []
    | _ => mkScene t [xAt (cm (-450)) 5, yNorth (cm 750) 4] [] [(1, 11)]

    (fun k => if k ≥ 2 then west10 else Build.west) (fun _ => Build.east)

    (fun _ => Build.west) (fun _ => Build.east)
    (fun k => match k with | 0 => [] | 1 => [(2, 10)] | _ => [(2, 13)])

    (fun _ => Build.west) (fun k => if k ≥ 2 then east10 else Build.east)

    (fun k => match k with | 0 => Build.west | 1 => west10 | _ => west20) (fun _ => Build.east)
    (fun k => match k with | 0 => [] | 1 => [(2, 10)] | _ => [(2, 13)])

    (fun _ => Build.west) (fun _ => Build.east)
    (fun k => match k with | 0 => [] | 1 => [(2, 10)] | _ => [(2, 13)])

/-
  Witnesses for NRS_484B_250_1.

  Geometry (metres, +x east, +y north): intersection i (10) is the square [-5, 5] × [-5, 5], lying on
  highways A (20, west of it), B (21, north–south) and C (22, east of it). Approach carriers, each
  entering i: cA (11) eastbound, x ∈ [-60, -5], y ∈ [-5, 0], on A; cB (12) northbound, x ∈ [0, 5],
  y ∈ [-60, -5], on B; cW (13) westbound, x ∈ [5, 60], y ∈ [0, 5], on C (A changes name to C across
  the junction, so cW is opposed to cA yet on a different highway).
  x (track 1) is a 4 m × 2 m car eastbound on cA at y = -2.5; y (track 2) is a car of the same size.
  Instants 1 s apart. A body across two regions has the second one stated in `occupies`.
  At x's entry (x at -4.5, 5 m/s) with y at (2.5, -4.5) northbound at 2 m/s, the predicted closest
  approach is about 0.74 m after about 1.34 s: well inside 4 m and 3 s. In the opposed scenes y
  runs westbound at y = 2.5, 5 m laterally from x: no conflict there, the exception decides.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Rules.NRS_484B.NRS_484B_250_1
import TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Builders

namespace TrafficSpecWitness.NRS_484B_250_1

open TrafficSpec

def m (n : Int) : Q := Units.metres n
def cm (n : Int) : Q := Units.centimetres n

-- Binders ↦ tracks: x ↦ 1

def iR : Structure :=
  { Build.rect 10 .intersection (m (-5)) (m (-5)) (m 5) (m 5) with ways := some [20, 21, 22] }
def cA : Structure :=
  { Build.lane 11 [(m (-60), m (-5)), (m (-5), m (-5)), (m (-5), m 0), (m (-60), m 0)] Build.east
      (enters := some 10) with ways := some [20] }
def cB : Structure :=
  { Build.lane 12 [(m 0, m (-60)), (m 5, m (-60)), (m 5, m (-5)), (m 0, m (-5))] Build.north
      (enters := some 10) with ways := some [21] }
def cW : Structure :=
  { Build.lane 13 [(m 5, m 0), (m 60, m 0), (m 60, m 5), (m 5, m 5)] Build.west
      (enters := some 10) with ways := some [22] }
def hA : Structure := Build.rect 20 .highway (m (-100)) (m (-5)) (m 5) (m 5)
def hB : Structure := Build.rect 21 .highway (m (-5)) (m (-100)) (m 5) (m 100)
def hC : Structure := Build.rect 22 .highway (m 5) (m (-5)) (m 100) (m 5)

def structs : List Structure := [iR, cA, cB, cW, hA, hB, hC]

def withYaw (u : RoadUser) (yaw : Q) : RoadUser :=
  Build.withKin u (fun k => { k with yawRate := some yaw })

/-- A unit heading given to 10⁻⁸ (cosine, sine of its angle). -/
def hdg (c s : Int) : Vec := (Units.ratio c 100000000, Units.ratio s 100000000)
/-- East turned 10° to the left; west turned 10° and 20° to the left. -/
def east10 : Vec := hdg 98480775 17364818
def west10 : Vec := hdg (-98480775) (-17364818)
def west20 : Vec := hdg (-93969262) (-34202014)

/-- x eastbound on cA at y = -2.5. -/
def xAt (px : Q) (speed : Int) (yaw : Int := 0) (heading : Vec := Build.east) : RoadUser :=
  withYaw (Build.user 1 [.motorVehicle] (px, cm (-250)) heading (Units.metresPerSecond speed) (m 2, m 1, m 1))
    (Units.degrees yaw)
/-- y northbound on cB at x = 2.5. -/
def yNorth (py : Q) (speed : Int) : RoadUser :=
  withYaw (Build.user 2 [.motorVehicle] (cm 250, py) Build.north (Units.metresPerSecond speed) (m 2, m 1, m 1))
    (Units.degrees 0)
/-- y westbound on cW at y = 0.5 (its right edge on the centre of the way, 3 m laterally from x). -/
def yWest (px : Q) (speed : Int) (yaw : Int := 0) (heading : Vec := Build.west) : RoadUser :=
  withYaw (Build.user 2 [.motorVehicle] (px, cm 50) heading (Units.metresPerSecond speed) (m 2, m 1, m 1))
    (Units.degrees yaw)
/-- z (track 3) northbound from cB at x = 2.5, 5 m/s: entered i at instant 0 and is leaving it
    northwards when x enters, its predicted closest approach to x over 9 m. -/
def zNorth (py : Q) : RoadUser :=
  withYaw (Build.user 3 [.motorVehicle] (cm 250, py) Build.north (Units.metresPerSecond 5) (m 2, m 1, m 1))
    (Units.degrees 0)

/-- A second intersection i2 (40) on highway B, 95 m north, and its northbound approach L2 (41). -/
def i2 : Structure :=
  { Build.rect 40 .intersection (m (-5)) (m 95) (m 5) (m 105) with ways := some [21] }
def l2 : Structure :=
  { Build.lane 41 [(m 0, m 60), (m 5, m 60), (m 5, m 95), (m 0, m 95)] Build.north
      (enters := some 40) with ways := some [21] }

def mkScene (t : Timestamp) (users : List RoadUser) (devices : List Device)
    (extra : List (TrackId × RegionId)) (intents : List DeclaredIntent := [])
    (more : List Structure := []) : Scene :=
  Build.scene t (some 1) users (structs ++ more) devices
    (occupies := some (Build.occupancyFromGeometry users (structs ++ more) ++ extra)) (intents := intents)

def turnLeft (who : TrackId) (v : Bool) : DeclaredIntent :=
  { vehicle := who, target := 10, values := [("int.turn_left", v)] }

/-- x on cA moving into i (entry at instant 2); y entered i from cB at instant 1 and crosses. -/
def crossingTrace (devices : List Device) (more : List Structure := []) : Trace :=
  Build.trace 3 0 (Units.seconds 1) fun k t =>
    match k with
    | 0 => mkScene t [xAt (cm (-1450)) 5, yNorth (cm (-850)) 2] devices [] (more := more)
    | 1 => mkScene t [xAt (cm (-950)) 5, yNorth (cm (-650)) 2] devices [(2, 10)] (more := more)
    | _ => mkScene t [xAt (cm (-450)) 5, yNorth (cm (-450)) 2] devices [(1, 11), (2, 12)] (more := more)

/-- `forbid` (violated): No device governs i or its approaches. x approaches on lane c (st.lane_enters c i, on highway A); y entered i from lane cy on highway B and is crossing. x moves into i; predicted closest approach 1 m in 1.5 s. -/
def forbidTrace : Trace := crossingTrace []

/-- `permit` (compliant): Same, but x halts on c while y crosses i and enters only after y has left. -/
def permitTrace : Trace :=
  Build.trace 5 0 (Units.seconds 1) fun k t =>
    match k with
    | 0 => mkScene t [xAt (cm (-1450)) 5, yNorth (cm (-850)) 4] [] []
    | 1 => mkScene t [xAt (cm (-950)) 0, yNorth (cm (-450)) 4] [] [(2, 12)]
    | 2 => mkScene t [xAt (cm (-950)) 0, yNorth (cm (-50)) 4] [] []
    | 3 => mkScene t [xAt (cm (-950)) 0, yNorth (cm 350) 4] [] []
    | _ => mkScene t [xAt (cm (-450)) 5, yNorth (cm 750) 4] [] [(1, 11)]

/-- `idle` (not_applicable): A dev.stop_sign governs c; the intersection is controlled by an official device and no signal is inoperative. -/
def idleTrace : Trace := crossingTrace [Build.sign 30 .stopSign [11]]

    instant; each heading is the previous one turned by its yaw rate over the 1 s interval. -/
def opposedTrace (yPos : Nat → Q) (ySpeed : Int) (yYaw xYaw : Nat → Int) (yHdg xHdg : Nat → Vec)
    (yExtra : Nat → List (TrackId × RegionId)) (intents : List DeclaredIntent)
    (withZ : Bool := false) : Trace :=

    let xPos := match k with | 0 => cm (-1450) | 1 => cm (-950) | _ => cm (-450)
    let xExtra : List (TrackId × RegionId) := if k ≥ 2 then [(1, 11)] else []
    let zs := if withZ then [zNorth (match k with | 0 => m (-6) | 1 => m (-1) | _ => m 4)] else []
    let zExtra : List (TrackId × RegionId) := if withZ && k == 0 then [(3, 10)] else []
    mkScene t ([xAt xPos 5 (xYaw k) (xHdg k), yWest (yPos k) ySpeed (yYaw k) (yHdg k)] ++ zs) []
      (xExtra ++ yExtra k ++ zExtra) intents

    (fun k => if k ≥ 2 then 10 else 0) (fun _ => 0)
    (fun k => if k ≥ 2 then west10 else Build.west) (fun _ => Build.east)

    (fun _ => Build.west) (fun k => if k ≥ 2 then east10 else Build.east)
    (fun k => match k with | 0 => [] | 1 => [] | _ => [(2, 10)])
